title: Molecular D\'ej\`a Vu: Digit-Level Retrieval of Published Values in Frontier Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2609.05381v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly evaluated on molecular property benchmarks, but accuracy cannot distinguish a model that predicts a property from one that retrieves a published number. We audit 22 frontier models on 12 regression benchmarks for verbatim retrieval and find that it is widespread but relatively benchmark-specific: on five datasets more than $50\%$ of the LLMs show verbatim retrieval, while on the remaining datasets it appears only in isolated cells. We run our experiments at two reasoning levels and find that reasoning changes retrieval. The same experiments, on the same molecules and with the same prompt, are flagged $89\%$ more often at the higher reasoning level than at the lowest one. Finally, we test a way to interrupt retrieval in our most contaminated cases, and find that the strongest models in some cases still recognise a combination of transformed SMILES strings and original labels. translated_title: 分子既视感：前沿语言模型对已发表数值的数字级检索
translated_abstract: 大语言模型越来越多地在分子性质基准上进行评估，但准确率无法区分一个模型是在真正预测性质还是在检索已发表的数值。我们对22个前沿模型在12个回归基准上进行了逐字检索审计，发现这种现象普遍存在但相对依赖于特定基准：在五个数据集中，超过50%的LLM表现出逐字检索行为，而在其余数据集中，这种现象仅在个别单元格中出现。我们在两个推理水平上进行实验，发现推理会改变检索行为——相同的实验、相同的分子、相同的提示词，在较高推理水平下被标记的频率比在最低推理水平下高出89%。最后，我们在污染最严重的案例中测试了一种中断检索的方法，发现最强的模型在某些情况下仍然能够识别经过转换的SMILES字符串与原始标签的组合。
tldr: 该论文首次系统审计了前沿大语言模型在分子性质基准上的数据污染问题，发现逐字检索已发表数值的现象普遍存在，且更强的推理能力会显著加剧这种检索行为。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically audits data contamination in frontier LLMs on molecular property benchmarks, revealing that verbatim retrieval of published values is widespread and that stronger reasoning significantly amplifies this retrieval behavior.
